To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the vascular smooth muscle cell has a high affinity, low capacity adenylyl-cyclase system and a high capacity, low affinity phosphodiesterase system; 2) the adenylyl- cyclase system is hormonally sensitive, and its hormonal sensitivity is lost in hypertensive disease; 3) the phosphodiesterase enzyme is hormonally insensitive, and its activity is increased in hypertensive disease.
hypertension may be a consequence of a loss of vascular adrenergic and angiotensin responsiveness.

the loss of hormonal sensitivity of vascular adeny-lyl cyclase activity and the elevation of phosphodiesterase levels may be the biochemical basis of the increased vascular tone and increased vascular smooth muscle cell proliferation that underlie the development and maintenance of hypertension.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the biochemical etiology and pathogenesis of hypertension.
elucidation of the biochemical etiology and pathogenesis of hypertension, and with the development of a novel therapeutic strategy based on the restoration of cyclic nucleotide homeostasis.
the role of nucleotides, especially cyclic nucleotides, in the pathogenesis of hypertension.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

cyclic GMP is a major mediator of the vascular changes that occur in hypertension and that the loss of adenylyl-cyclase hormonal sensitivity is an important early event in the development of the hypertensive state.
the cyclic AMP: cyclic GMP ratio in the vasomotor system is the most fundamental determinant of blood pressure.
cyclic nucleotides play a central role in the development and progression of hypertension.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

hypertension is the end result of a series of events that are initiated by increased sympathetic nerve activity or increased renin-angio- tensin levels and which are maintained by a series of events involving the loss of vascular adenosine cyclase hormonal sensitivity, increased phosphodiesterases, increased vascular cyclic GMP:AMP ratio, increased vascular smooth muscle sensitivity, and increased vascular smooth muscle tone.
the cyclic AMP system in the vasculatures of spontaneously hypertensive rats is defective.

the loss of vascular adenosine 3',5'-monophosphate (cAMP) responsiveness is the primary biochemical lesion in hypertension and that this lesion can be reversed by treatment with drugs that increase vascular cAMP.
The main takeaway from our work is that
cyclic nucleotides play important roles in the pathogenesis of hypertension.
cyclic nucleotide abnormalities in hypertension are not just an epiphenomenon, but may play a central role in the pathophysiology of hypertension.
the loss of adenylyl cyclic nucleotide hormonal sensitivity is a major contributor to the development of hypertension and the associated vascular pathology.
